title: Pictograms / Color treatments — Dark background

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: Dark background

slide_intent: Distinguish decorative treatment from the symbol’s core shape, because color should add expression without preventing immediate recognition.
strategic_value: A bounded set of monochrome, tonal and gradient options can let IBM pictograms vary while remaining part of one family.
demonstration: Four pictograms on a dark-purple field compare a white-line symbol, a purple outline, a shaded purple symbol and a blue-purple gradient robot arm. The first white specimen retains the source caption Black.
practical_value: Compare the four treatments on a dark field while relying on the actual artwork and surrounding guidance rather than the mismatched first caption.

content_islands.name: Background selector
content_islands.spec: Show Dark background selected above the field.

content_islands.name: Treatment comparison
content_islands.spec: Align four specimens with the source captions Black, Color, Tinted color and Gradient, preserving the first caption’s mismatch with the white linework.

reference_purposes.Expression: The row demonstrates four pictogram color treatments against one dark background.
reference_purposes.Application: The accompanying color guidance identifies black/white, monochromatic, tinted/shaded and gradient options.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying design guidance requires pictograms to meet 4.5:1 contrast regardless of style; the screenshot’s first caption is a source-label inconsistency, not a black-on-dark recommendation.
